The absorbing screen achieves 68.1% relative bandwidth at 0 eV chemical potential, significantly wider than conventional absorbers.
The total thickness of the screen is 3.4 mm, which is only 0.15λ at the central frequency of 13.5 GHz.
Graphene surface conductivity changes from 0.9 mS to more than 9 mS as chemical potential varies from 0 to 0.4 eV in the microwave band.
The Hilbert curve metal strips are made of copper with electrical conductivity of 5.96×10⁷ S/m.
Three resonant frequencies identified are 11.19 GHz, 13.44 GHz, and 16.64 GHz at 0 eV chemical potential.
The silicon dioxide layer thickness is 50 nm and polysilicon layer thickness is 50 nm in the tuning structure.
The dielectric layers D1 and D2 have a dielectric constant of 4.3 and are made of the same material.
At 0 eV chemical potential with 0 V applied voltage, the central frequency is 13.5 GHz with 9.2 GHz effective absorption bandwidth.
At 0.4 eV chemical potential (30.7 V applied), the central frequency shifts to 19.0 GHz with 7.8 GHz effective absorption bandwidth.
The Rozanov theoretical thickness limit for this design is calculated to be 3.1 mm, and the actual design is only 0.3 mm thicker.
The graphene sheet is modeled with electro-phonon relaxation time τ = 0.2 ps at temperature T = 300 K.
The -10 dB absorption bandwidth spans from 8.9 GHz to 18.1 GHz at 0 eV chemical potential.
The metal strip width is 0.1 mm and the Hilbert curve dimension is 2 mm in the optimized design.
Graphene surface impedance is approximately 1.2 kΩ at 0 eV, 420 Ω at 0.1 eV, and 110 Ω at 0.4 eV.
The free space characteristic impedance is 377 Ω, making graphene impedance values suitable for impedance matching.
Without the graphene sheet, the metal strip array alone produces only narrow absorption peaks with very limited bandwidth.
The power dissipation density in the graphene is calculated using Pd = (1/2)∫σₛ|E|² dv, showing strong absorption near metal strips.
The carrier density of graphene can be modified by external voltage through the relationship nₛ = ε₀εₜVDC/te.
The design uses e-beam lithography to pattern metal strips on the graphene surface during fabrication.
The structure includes a perfect electric conductor (PEC) ground to eliminate transmission and maximize absorption.
Dielectric losses have minimal impact on absorption performance, confirming that graphene is the primary absorption mechanism.
The design achieves near-minimum thickness limitation for non-magnetic absorbers according to Rozanov's theorem.
The graphene sheet is transferred onto the dielectric stack after fabrication of the polysilicon and silicon dioxide layers.
The top dielectric layer D1 can be bonded using adhesive bonding film with thickness less than 1 mil under thermal compression.
